title: BCI-FIT: A customization protocol for communication brain-computer interface systems.
description: EEG recordings from five participants with speech and/or physical impairments due to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) who used a non-implantable communication brain-computer interface (cBCI) over multiple visits. Participants completed calibration and copy-spelling tasks with Matrix and RSVP layouts, in both customized and non-customized system configurations. Customization was iteratively adjusted based on typing performance, preferences, clinical observations, brain signal characteristics, and offline simulations. The data are organized in BIDS format.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with Wearable Sensing dry-electrode caps (DSI-Flex or DSI-24) via Lab Streaming Layer at 300 Hz, then downsampled to 150 Hz and filtered at 1-20 Hz with a 60 Hz notch. Tasks were run with BciPy 2.0 using Matrix and RSVP typing layouts. Calibration used 55 inquiries of 14 characters presented at 5 Hz. Copy-spelling required participants to copy five-letter words, with adaptive stopping based on a classifier confidence threshold of 0.8.
